newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close up a touch, News dips.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close up a touch, News dips.

text.p: Australian shares ended a subdued session slightly firmer on Wednesday, the continuing decline of News Corp since its first quarter results on Tuesday holding back the market which nervously eyed a buoyant Wall Street.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 3.4 points higher at 2,346.9 after touching an intra-day low of 2,337.5.
December share price index futures closed just one point firmer 2,348 and at a slim 1.3 point premium to the index.
News Corp shares dipped again as U.S. broker Goldman Sachs downgraded the stock after the company's first quarter results disappointed investors.
"It was a curious day. A couple of issues like News Corp and Amcor camouflaged good gains from BHP," a Perth dealer said.
"Investors, naturally, are still worried about a possible Dow pullback, but there were signs today that the resolve of some players was starting to weaken," the dealer said

One of the most sought after stocks was the recently listed Papua New Guinean (PNG) company Orogen Minerals whose shares continued to rise following some promising results from an onshore PNG oil exploration well on Tuesday.
Orogen is the holding company for the resource assets of the PNG government's Mineral Resources Developement Corp.
Australian bonds saw a sharp rally following a strong U.S. market. The yield on 10 year T-bonds finished at 7.09 percent, down 0.08 percentage points from Tuesday's close.
The Australian dollar finished little changed after a sleepy session as a dearth of domestic features left traders little to do but second guess samurai issues.
By 4.50 pm (0650 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7880/85.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Turnover on both options and futures markets remained modest in line with the physical market.
Total options traded 35,149 (38,535)
